item.text: I’m replacing the current dynamic bucket object model with a simpler two-pass layout: count first, allocate exact bucket sizes once, then fill/sort/merge. That should reduce internal complexity instead of just moving it around.
I’ve confirmed the current shape. I’m cutting out the `BucketSet`/`Bucket` state machine entirely and replacing it with count/allocate/fill helpers so the algorithm reads straight through.
The algorithm is flatter now. I’m adding one more edge-case test around the lower bound so the value-range contract is covered on both sides.
I’ve finished the edit set. Compiling and running the demo plus tests now to verify the two-pass bucket layout and the added lower-bound coverage.

Refactored [BucketSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSort.java:1) to remove the internal `BucketSet`/`Bucket` object graph entirely. The sorter now uses a simpler two-pass flow: count values per bucket, allocate exact bucket arrays once, distribute with insertion indexes, sort each bucket, then merge back. That makes the algorithm easier to read and removes the dynamic bucket-resizing logic.

I also extended [BucketSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSortTest.java:1) with explicit lower-bound coverage for `0.0f`, so the supported range is now tested on both ends.
